lead.hed: Destroyer USS Spruance passes 342 days at sea, the longest Navy destroyer deployment since World War II
lead.insight: Defense News reported Oct. 29 that the Arleigh Burke-class destroyer had reached 342 days deployed after leaving San Diego with the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group on Nov. 21, 2025. Navy leaders say extended deployments will remain common while ships returning from operations enter a maintenance system already carrying years of accumulated delays.

political.hed: Pentagon officials ask Baltic allies to temper public rhetoric about Russia
political.insight: Defense News and Reuters report that U.S. officials privately urged Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to use more measured language as Washington renews its push for negotiations over Ukraine. A Pentagon spokesman declined to discuss private allied talks, and the Baltic defense ministries did not comment.

political.hed: Hanwha's Philadelphia yard wins the first Landing Ship Medium construction award
political.insight: USNI News reports that TOTE Services awarded Hanwha Philly Shipyard a $269 million contract to build the Marine Corps' Landing Ship Medium. TOTE holds the Navy's $2.2 billion vessel-construction-manager contract for the program.

tech.hed: France turns tank gunners into FPV pilots and plans 15 drone-combat units by summer 2027
tech.insight: France's 1st Marine Infantry Regiment converted a light-cavalry squadron into a dedicated drone unit after exercises showed small FPV teams could disrupt armored formations and command posts. Army leaders are scaling the model while warning that weather, jamming, and a lack of riflemen still limit drone-only formations.

tech.hed: Ukraine finishes its share of Freyja missile defense as European components become the bottleneck
tech.insight: Ukraine says its FP-7.X interceptor and launcher work is complete, while partner companies continue integrating radars, seekers, fire control, and a command center. The coalition is aiming for initial tests by year's end, but the seeker remains the hardest piece and battlefield use is targeted for next July.

tech.hed: Providence warns cheap autonomous weapons can make long wars politically easier to sustain
tech.insight: The essay argues that inexpensive, attritable drones can spare troops while lowering the public and political cost of continuing a conflict. It calls for stronger congressional oversight and public moral justification when presidents exercise war powers in an age of increasingly autonomous battlefields.

culture.hed: American Reformer reviews Michael Anton's account of California's political decline
culture.insight: Colin Redemer opens with California's long dependence on migration, then notes that net migration turned negative around 2017. His review uses Anton's Dispatches from the Late Republic to examine how the state's promise of mobility and prosperity gave way to outward flight.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Washington Irving gave a young republic its ghosts
culture.insight: The essay reads The Legend of Sleepy Hollow as an early statement of American identity, rooted in the Hudson Valley's Revolutionary War memory. Irving answered doubts about whether the new republic could produce great literature by turning its own landscape and history into material.
